description:
Give your AI agent a real browser. This walkthrough shows how to extend Pi with Steel's browser extension, then demos it running two tasks end-to-end: comparing every MacBook model from Apple.com and pulling the latest API docs from OpenAI's Cloudflare-protected site. All powered by Z.AI's GLM 5.1 with medium reasoning.

What's covered:
  - Installing the Steel extension for Pi with a single pi install command
  - Giving Pi scraping, screenshots, and full computer actions through Steel
  - Demo: comparing all current MacBook models by self-discovering links across Apple.com
  - How Pi handles heavy, agent-unfriendly pages with screenshots and content extraction
  - Demo: navigating OpenAI's Cloudflare-protected docs to find the latest model usage
  - Getting back structured reports with implementation examples grounded in live documentation
  - Output as Markdown, HTML, or screenshots depending on the task
  - Using Steel for competitor monitoring, PDF scraping, and change tracking

Pi is a general-purpose agent, not a browser-specific one. It just gets a small set of browser tools via Steel and figures out the rest. Point it at a task, let GLM 5.1 reason through the navigation, and get a structured report back.

To install it just run: pi install npm:@steel-experiments/pi-steel
If you don't have Pi: npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent

Steel: https://steel.dev
Z.ai: https://z.ai
GitHub: https://github.com/steel-experiments/pi-steel
GitHub: https://github.com/steel-dev/steel-browser

Key Moments:
0:00 – Pi agent intro
0:47 – MacBook comparison demo
2:30 – Report generation
3:26 – OpenAI docs demo
4:57 – Final output
5:10 – Wrap-up
